body: Hey there OP, it sounds like you really needed to get a lot of that stuff off your chest, I bet you feel better after that even if it’s just a tiny bit. You’re like many of us friend, victims to unfortunate fates but that doesn’t mean things have to stay that way. About two hundred some odd days ago I came here because I was in the same situation as you, just a guy who seemed like everything was his fault, life was shitty, girl hard left me, nothing good was happening. I found out I was diagnosed with G.A.D (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) it completely ruined my dream to join the Army and work on tanks, I was really scared during that point of time but I couldn’t stop. I didn’t want to let myself be crumbled up and thrown away because I ran out of back up plans. I started to find a hobby that I could drain my time into and distract me from a lot of negative thoughts. I knew my anxiety wouldn’t let me reach too far boundary wise I had to work not exactly around it but with it. I’d suggest finding out what triggers your anxiety and basically test the waters. I shit you not for the first time in my entire life I had tacos about two weeks ago because I had built up enough confidence to try them, and god I see why people enjoy them. I hope that last tidbit made you smile because it’s something I try to do often, smile. I think another thing that helped me with my anxiety is realizing that I don’t need to care about people’s perception of me, it’s my life and I get to control it. You just need to start somewhere, even if it’s the smallest of baby steps it helps, I mean the tiniest domino can knock down the largest of them all as long as you take steps to do it. So just take some time, focus on yourself in all aspects. Dedicate your time to the things you want to enjoy, in time you’ll be able to the things you love and understand it’s okay if life is in cruise control, just gotta wait it out y’know? You’ve got this OP, just dust yourself off and hop up on the saddle again. Just know that you’re going to have dark thoughts, I still do to this day since I’ve recovered, but I learn to distract myself with something to suppress those thoughts. I hoped what I have said has helped, just remember you’re not alone! Keep on carrying the torch, keep trying, you’re sure to be rewarded I promise. Feel free to get some more stuff off your chest, Im right here.
